Scenario: GitHub repo secrets CSDOCS_SANDBOX_STACK_API_KEY, CSDOCS_SANDBOX_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN, PROD_CSDOCS_STACK_API_KEY, PROD_CSDOCS_STACK_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN are all set
Expected Result: All 3 workflow files use these exact names consistently. If any is missing, loadConfig() throws immediately

Scenario: Local .env uses a different naming convention (SANDBOX_CONTENTSTACK_DOCS_STACK_API_KEY / CONTENTSTACK_DOCS_STACK_API_KEY) than CI does
Expected Result: Not a bug, but anyone testing locally must map/rename env vars manually or scripts fail with 'Missing required credentials'

Scenario: Sandbox docs_article schema still matches Prod's (rerun the schema diff script)
Expected Result: Confirms nobody has edited the Sandbox schema again since the fix

Scenario: New .md file added under cs-docs/assets/<subfolder>/ with H1 matching frontmatter title
Expected Result: Sandbox entry created, article_content populated from H1+body, seo populated, tagged nav-subsection-<subfolder> and pr-<PR#>

Scenario: Existing file's content edited (no rename)
Expected Result: Sandbox entry updated in place, no new tags added (tags only apply on create)

Scenario: File moved to a new path with the same content
Expected Result: handleRename fires. If the old entry can be found, it is updated in place (url changes, uid stays) with action:renamed. Confirm no duplicate is created

Scenario: File deleted
Expected Result: Sandbox entry is unpublished, not deleted. Confirm the entry still exists in Sandbox as a draft, just no longer live

Scenario: File added outside cs-docs/assets/ (e.g. cs-docs/personalize/)
Expected Result: Skipped silently, no error, run does not fail (resolveProductConfig returns null)

Scenario: File with a doc_type not in the docs_article set (reference-only type)
Expected Result: Skipped silently, no error

Scenario: File missing an H1 heading entirely
Expected Result: Run fails with "missing a top-level H1 heading"

Scenario: File where frontmatter title does not match the H1 text
Expected Result: Run fails with the title/H1 mismatch error

Scenario: Frontmatter description under 120 or over 165 characters
Expected Result: Lint fails before sync even runs (npm run lint)

Scenario: A file's frontmatter url changes but the file path does not move
Expected Result: Confirm the fallback lookup (by old url via beforeSha) finds and updates the right entry, not a duplicate

Scenario: Local image referenced in the markdown (e.g. ![alt](./img.png))
Expected Result: Image uploaded to Sandbox Assets, markdown rewritten to the CDN URL, local file removed from the repo after the run

Scenario: Nested folder depth (2+ levels deep)
Expected Result: Confirm detection still works, this was the bug Gladys originally reported and it could not be reproduced, worth one more real-world check

Scenario: Push with multiple files changed at once, some in scope and some not
Expected Result: In-scope files sync, out-of-scope files skip, one bad file does not block the good ones

Scenario: Brand-new Sandbox entry, published, never promoted before
Expected Result: Created in Prod, published to Staging, breadcrumb populated with the Prod-side UID, linked into nav, added to a new Release

Scenario: Same entry promoted again with no content change
Expected Result: Skipped with "no changes detected", confirms contentsEqual stays stable now that breadcrumb is remapped before comparison

Scenario: Sandbox entry content edited after already being promoted once
Expected Result: Prod entry updated in place, republished to Staging, not re-added to nav or a new Release (nav-linking only fires on create)

Scenario: Sandbox entry that has never been published (still a draft)
Expected Result: Not included in the promotion batch at all (getPublishedEntries only returns published entries)

Scenario: Sandbox entry whose publish_details is in a shape the code cannot parse a version out of
Expected Result: Marked "unresolved", promotion refuses and logs the PUBLISH_SHAPE_HELP message rather than guessing which version to promote

Scenario: KNOWN GAP: a Sandbox entry gets renamed (see 1.3), producing a Prod url change
Expected Result: Because Prod matching is purely by url, the promotion script will not find the old Prod entry by the new url and will create a second duplicate Prod entry instead of updating the original
Priority/Notes: Needs a decision before wider rollout

Scenario: KNOWN GAP: a doc is deleted from GitHub (see 1.4), Sandbox entry unpublished
Expected Result: The already-promoted Prod entry is never unpublished; deletions do not cascade to Prod today
Priority/Notes: Confirm acceptable or flag as follow-up

Scenario: apidocs stack entries are promoted in the same run
Expected Result: Confirm they are handled through the completely separate apidocs code path and are unaffected by any of the csdocs changes made this round

Scenario: Multiple entries promoted in a single run, one of them errors (e.g. Prod url ambiguous match)
Expected Result: The one bad entry fails and is logged, the rest of the batch still processes

Scenario: New doc under a subfolder matching an existing nav_section.header (e.g. overview/)
Expected Result: Link appended to that section's existing links[], no duplicate, no other links disturbed

Scenario: New doc under a brand-new subfolder with no matching nav section yet
Expected Result: A new nav_section block is created with a title-cased header (e.g. custom-workflows becomes "Custom Workflows")

Scenario: New doc under a product folder other than assets
Expected Result: Linking is skipped with a clear reason logged (no verified product_navigation mapping for "X"), does not fail the whole promotion

Scenario: New doc missing its nav-subsection-* tag (should not happen via normal flow)
Expected Result: Linking skipped with reason logged, not silently guessed

Scenario: One new doc promoted and linked into nav successfully
Expected Result: Release named "PR #<number>" created, containing both the docs_article entry and the product_navigation entry

Scenario: New doc promoted but nav linking failed or was skipped
Expected Result: Release still created, but contains only the docs_article entry

Scenario: Entry has no pr-<number> tag (e.g. pushed directly to main with no PR)
Expected Result: No Release created, logged as skipped, promotion itself still succeeds

Scenario: Two different PRs each add a doc
Expected Result: both promoted in the same run
Priority/Notes: Two separate Releases created, one per PR number, not merged into one

Scenario: Production environment (not Staging) is never published to by any script in this pipeline
Expected Result: Verify by checking Prod entries' publish_details after a full run, only staging should appear

Scenario: No script in this pipeline ever calls a Prod delete endpoint
Expected Result: Confirmed by design (ProdPromoteClient has no delete method), worth a code-level re-check before handover

Scenario: A completely unrelated product folder (e.g. cs-docs/launch/) sees zero behavior change from this round's work
